AccessibilityNode.description:
One element.

`states` is a list rather than OSWorld's `st:foo="true"` attribute-presence
encoding: the same information, and JSON has a list type where XML
attributes do not.

actions.description:
Action names the element supports: control patterns on Windows
(`invoke`, `toggle`, `select`, `expand_collapse`), the application's own
names on Linux (`click`, `press`, `activate`, ...). `set_value` appears
on both when the element accepts `NODE_SET_VALUE`; the other names are
what `NODE_INVOKE` accepts.

oneOf.description:
`None` when the element is offscreen or has no geometry — absent rather
than zeroed, because `0,0 0x0` is a real rectangle and would be acted on.

node_id.description:
Backend handle: `a:<bus name>:<object path>` on AT-SPI,
`u:<runtime id>` on UI Automation. Valid for as long as the element
exists — across snapshots — so it can be resolved later by
`GET /v2/computer/accessibility/nodes?node_id=` and acted on by the
`NODE_*` display actions. An element that has gone (its window closed,
its application restarted) resolves to 404: take a fresh snapshot.

role.description:
Raw, as the backend reports it. Not normalised into a cross-platform
vocabulary: a lossy rename would be a second thing to be wrong about,
and consumers already handle per-platform roles.

AccessibilityNodeList.description: A flat search result: the matching nodes without their subtrees.

nodes.description: In tree order. `children` is always empty here.

truncated.description:
True when `limit`, a node budget or the timeout stopped the search
before the whole scope was seen.

display_generation.description:
Bumped whenever the desktop geometry changes, which invalidates every
outstanding coordinate at once rather than one node at a time.

AccessibilityWindow.description: One window's subtree plus how well it could be read.

truncated.description:
True when a depth or node budget stopped the walk, so a consumer knows
the absence of a node is not evidence the node does not exist.

screenshot.description:
Post-action screenshot (base64 PNG), present only when requested via
`?include_screenshot=true`. aiod-only increment over the Python
contract: folds the act→observe round-trip of computer-use loops
into one request.

screenshot_error.description:
Why the post-action screenshot is absent, when one was asked for and
could not be taken. The action itself already happened — reporting the
capture failure as a failure of the whole call would invite a retry that
clicks or types a second time.

user.description:
Account to run as; absent uses AIO_DEFAULT_USER, then aiod's own account
when no default is configured. Recorded on the session the first time it
is seen and fixed thereafter — passing a different one to an existing
session is a 400, not a silent identity change. Linux only.

output.description:
`stdout` followed by `stderr`, as a caller reading a single stream
expects to see them. A deliberate superset of the 1.0 contract, whose
`BashExecResult` carried only the two separate streams: agentkit's
`_handle_hot_update_response` reads `data.output`, so serving only
`stdout`/`stderr` leaves that client with nothing to read.

stdout_gap.description:
True when the request's offset fell before the retained start: the
bytes in between are gone and `stdout` begins at the retained tail,
not at the requested position.

stdout_start_offset.description:
Earliest logical stdout position still retained; everything before it
was trimmed by the 10 MiB per-stream retention cap.

user.description: Account every command in this session runs as. Linux only.

bash.description:
Resolved `bash` — null where no bash exists. Never a stand-in for
another shell: a client that reads this field to build a `bash -c`
invocation must not be handed `pwsh.exe`, which parses nothing the
same way. The shell actually backing `/v1/bash` on such a platform is
reported below.

cmd.description: Resolved cmd.exe, the `shell: "cmd"` selector's target. Windows only.

powershell.description:
Resolved PowerShell, on platforms where it backs `/v1/bash`. Null on
Unix (additive field; absent from the 1.0 contract).

executable_source.description: Where the executable was found: env | wellknown | path.

BrowserInfoResult.description:
The browser control plane's self-description. The daemon does not serve a
VNC stack — that is the image/gateway layer's business — so `vnc_url` is
reported on the v1 plane alone, where the 1.x client model requires it.

cdp_ui_url.description:
URL of the bundled CDP viewer page, or null when no such page is
installed — the daemon only advertises a UI it can serve itself.

vnc_url.description:
URL of the noVNC page the deployment installs, empty when it installs
none. Absent (not null) outside the v1 plane, whose 1.x model requires
the field and rejects a null.

browser.description:
Daemon-native probe: the browser control plane is a CDP client over
localhost, so the daemon inspects it directly rather than relaying.

tab_id.description: Route to a specific page target (default: the active page).

ref.description: Snapshot element ref (B-class path: a real click via Input events).

selector.description: CSS selector of the element (A-class path).

ClipboardContents.description:
Clipboard contents.

`format` is carried from v1 even though `text` is the only value it can
take, so that adding an image clipboard later is an addition rather than a
breaking change — an image needs its own encoding and a media type, and a
bare `{"text": …}` would have no room for either.

backend.description:
Which layer runs **python on the code surfaces** (`/v1/code`, `/v2/code`):
`"endpoint"` (a reachable `AIO_JUPYTER_ENDPOINT`), `"kernel"` (the
daemon's embedded `ipykernel` client), or `"native"` (the embedded REPL).
Absent when no python runs there at all. Normally the same ladder
`jupyter_backend` reports; `AIO_CODE_BACKEND` can pin this one alone, and
then the two fields disagree on purpose. Additive field — clients reading
the 1.0 shape ignore it.

default_python.description:
The python interpreter the daemon-native tier actually runs here, after
`PYTHON_VERSION`/`PYTHON_CODE_EXEC_VERSION`. Additive field, and the
answer to "did my version selection take effect" — the one question the
env mouths otherwise leave a client guessing about.

endpoint.description:
The `AIO_JUPYTER_ENDPOINT` that is answering, when one is. `None` when
python runs inside this daemon.

javascript_backend.description:
Which layer runs **javascript**: always `"native"`, because the kernel is
python-only and an endpoint is a python server. Absent when `node` is not
installed. Stated rather than implied — `backend` says nothing about it,
and a client that reads one field for both would be told the wrong thing
the moment python leaves the daemon.

jupyter_backend.description:
Which layer answers `/v1/jupyter`: the python `backend`, minus
`"native"` — a REPL cannot speak the kernel protocol, so that plane is
absent rather than downgraded.

kinds.description:
The families this daemon serves: `code` (either language), `nodejs`, and
`jupyter` when python has a kernel or an endpoint behind it.

python_kernels.description:
`kernel_name` values `/v1/jupyter` accepts here, default first. Empty
when the embedded kernel tier is not the one answering.

args.description:
argv for `shell: "none"`; rejected for shell modes, where quoting
belongs to the script.

command.description: The script to run — or, with `shell: "none"`, the program path.

env.description: Per-command env; overrides same-named keys from the session's env.

session.description: Session to run in; absent = an anonymous session reclaimed on idle.

user.description:
Account to run as; recorded on the session the first time it is seen
and fixed thereafter. Linux only.

env.description: Session-wide env, inherited by every command; per-command env wins.

user.description: Account every command in this session runs as. Linux only.

allOf.description:
Writing is an action; *reading* is `GET /v2/computer/clipboard`.

The split is not arbitrary: an action response carries only status
(`action_performed` plus an optional screenshot), so it has no channel
to return data through — data comes from noun routes. Writing belongs
here rather than on a route of its own so it composes in a batch, which
is the whole point: a paste is "set the clipboard, then Ctrl+V", and any
round trip between those two steps is a window for the focus to move.

oneOf.description:
Writing is an action; *reading* is `GET /v2/computer/clipboard`.

The split is not arbitrary: an action response carries only status
(`action_performed` plus an optional screenshot), so it has no channel
to return data through — data comes from noun routes. Writing belongs
here rather than on a route of its own so it composes in a batch, which
is the whole point: a paste is "set the clipboard, then Ctrl+V", and any
round trip between those two steps is a window for the focus to move.

allOf.description:
Raise and focus. One action, not two: on both platforms "activate" and
"focus" resolve to the same operation at this level, and publishing two
names for one behaviour would make the contract lie about what the
second one does.

oneOf.description:
Raise and focus. One action, not two: on both platforms "activate" and
"focus" resolve to the same operation at this level, and publishing two
names for one behaviour would make the contract lie about what the
second one does.

allOf.description:
Act on an accessibility node instead of a coordinate. The handle comes
from `GET /v2/computer/accessibility` or `.../accessibility/nodes` and
stays valid while the element exists. These run in the same worker
turn as pointer and keyboard input, so a batch can focus a field
through the tree and then `TYPING` into it.

oneOf.description:
Act on an accessibility node instead of a coordinate. The handle comes
from `GET /v2/computer/accessibility` or `.../accessibility/nodes` and
stays valid while the element exists. These run in the same worker
turn as pointer and keyboard input, so a batch can focus a field
through the tree and then `TYPING` into it.

allOf.description:
Run one of the node's `actions` (the first one when `action` is
omitted). Answers 409 for a name the node does not advertise.

oneOf.description:
Run one of the node's `actions` (the first one when `action` is
omitted). Answers 409 for a name the node does not advertise.

allOf.description:
Set a text or numeric value directly through the accessibility API.
No key events are generated; an application that only reacts to typing
needs `NODE_FOCUS` + `TYPING` instead.

oneOf.description:
Set a text or numeric value directly through the accessibility API.
No key events are generated; an application that only reacts to typing
needs `NODE_FOCUS` + `TYPING` instead.

DisplayActionBatchRequest.description:
A sequence of actions run in one call. Additive: the single-action body
stays exactly what the 1.0 contract describes, so this is a second shape
rather than a change to the first one — which also keeps the precise 422 a
single action gets for a missing `action_type`.

include_screenshot.description: Return a screenshot taken after the last action that ran.

failed_index.description: Index of the action that failed, if one did. Everything before it ran.

reason.description: Machine-readable cause of that refusal, e.g. `secure-desktop-or-uipi`.

screenshot_error.description:
Why it is absent, when one was asked for and failed. Same reasoning as
the single-action envelope: the sequence already ran.

status.description:
`"denied"` when the sequence stopped because the host *refused* the
input rather than failing to deliver it. Absent otherwise.

A batch answers 200 even when it stops early — the actions before the
failure really ran — so the refusal has to be reportable inside the
body. Same `status`/`reason` pair the single-action path returns as a
403.

await_promise.description: Await a returned Promise before replying.

expression.description: JavaScript expression evaluated in the page's main world.

value.description: The JSON value the expression produced (by-value).

overwrite.description: Replace an existing destination. Off by default.

recursive.description:
Also delete non-empty directories (like `rm -r`). Without it, only
files, symlinks and empty directories are removed.

truncated.description: Set when the internal result cap was hit; the listing is incomplete.

is_hidden.description:
Hidden by the platform's convention: a dot name, or on Windows the
Hidden/System attribute (what keeps `desktop.ini` out of Explorer).
Present only when true.

truncated.description: Set when the internal entry cap was hit; the listing is incomplete.

parents.description:
Create missing parent directories (like `mkdir -p`), and succeed if
the directory already exists.

created.description: False when `parents=true` and the directory already existed.

overwrite.description:
Replace an existing destination. Off by default so a rename can never
silently clobber.

sudo.description:
Compatibility spelling of `user: "root"`. Validated, then used as an
ownership identity: the operation executes with daemon privileges and
anything it creates is owned by root.

selector.description: CSS selector of the input/textarea/contenteditable (A-class path).

FsEditRequest.description:
The editor request as v2 states it: the three commands that survive the
admission test, and only the fields they use. The v1 model carries the
openhands-era baggage (`file_text`, `view_range`, `page_range`,
`sheet_name`, `row_range`, `slide_range`, `enable_metadata`,
`enable_linting`) that belongs to the rejected commands or to document
formats this server does not parse; none of it is reachable from here.

`command` is a `String`, not an enum, on purpose: a rejected value must
come back as a 400 that names the route to use instead, and an enum would
turn `view` into an anonymous 422 deserialization failure before any
handler could say where to go.

new_str.description: `str_replace`: the replacement. `insert`: the text to insert.

replace_mode.description:
`str_replace`: `ALL` | `FIRST` | `LAST`. Absent means the anchor must
match exactly once, and a second occurrence is an error rather than a
silent choice.

pattern.description: Glob matched against file names/paths under `path`.

accessibility.description: Whether the semantic tree can be read right now.

accessibility_backend.description:
Which backend would read it — `"uia"`, `"atspi"`, or `null` where none is
compiled. Reported alongside the liveness flag rather than folded into
it: `false` + `"atspi"` means "this host is not set up", while `false` +
`null` means "this build cannot", and the fix differs.

provider.description: Reserved for the provider seam (external | xvfb-lite).

revision.description:
Commit this binary was built from. `version` is the crate version and is
identical across builds of different commits, so it can prove the server
is alive but never which build is answering.

MatchMode.description: How `role` and `name` are compared. Case-insensitive in every mode.

tab_id.description: Target a specific tab; defaults to the active page.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for that event before giving up.

url.description: Absolute URL to open. Mutually exclusive with `history`.
URL to open in the new tab; defaults to `about:blank`.

NodeBounds.description:
A rectangle in absolute desktop pixels.

Both backends already report screen coordinates — UIA's `BoundingRectangle`
and AT-SPI's `getExtents(XY_SCREEN)` — so this needs no per-platform
translation, which is the property that lets one DTO carry both.

action.description: One of the node's `actions`; the first one when omitted.

NodeRefAction.description: Addresses a node from an accessibility snapshot or search.

value.description: Text for editable text, a number for ranges (sliders, spin buttons).

NodeSource.description:
Where a node came from. Carried per node, not per tree, because a single
snapshot can mix sources once vision-inferred nodes exist — and a consumer
that trusts them equally is exactly the failure the plane design warns
about ("wrong structure is worse than none").

NodeValue.description: A numeric range, when the element exposes one.

env.description: Not implemented yet — rejected rather than ignored.

retention.description:
`persistent` (explicit delete; tmux-backed where available) or
`expiring` (idle reclaim). Default persistent — creating by id *is*
the persistence opt-in.

user.description: Account the terminal's shell runs as; fixed for the session's life.

data.description:
What one v2 environment call answers with: the identity and directory
fields the v1 sandbox route reports, plus the capability probe that used to
need a second request. Merging them is the point of the route — a client
bootstraps with one round trip instead of five.

capabilities.description:
The same snapshot the capabilities route serves: which planes have a
backend on this host, and the binaries behind them.

workspace_dir.description:
Wire-compat names for one value: the daemon account's home, which is
where a command that names no working directory runs.

ref.description:
Stable element ref usable by click/fill/upload for the life of the
snapshot (the page's backend DOM node id). Absent for structural nodes.

truncated.description:
Root only: the page exceeded [`AX_MAX_NODES`] or [`AX_MAX_DEPTH`], so
what came back is a prefix of the tree, not the tree. Omitted when the
whole page fit, which keeps an untruncated snapshot byte-identical to
the shape clients already parse.

entries.description:
Entries written. For a merge this counts the merged entries, not the
entries already present in the destination.

mode.description:
`rename` when the destination did not exist and the staged tree was
claimed whole, `merge` when it did and entries were overlaid one by one.

path.description: Destination directory the archive was extracted into.

initial_cursor.description:
Where a consumer that wants "events from now on" starts polling.

`cursor: 0` deliberately means "replay the buffered history" — but a
reused watcher (`reused: true`) has history, and a client that lost
its cursor had no way to say "only the future" without receiving it
all again. Fresh watcher: 0. Reused: the current latest seq.

The image's pre-baked unprivileged account, as it actually resolved at
container start — not as the build args asked for it.

where a command that names no working directory runs. The daemon has no

cookies.description:
One or more cookies (CDP `Network.CookieParam` shape: `name`, `value`,
and `url` or `domain`+`path`, plus optional `expires`, `httpOnly`,
`secure`, `sameSite`).

user.description: Account this terminal's shell runs as; see ShellExecRequest::user.

Account to run this terminal's shell as; absent uses AIO_DEFAULT_USER,
then aiod's own account when no default is configured.
Per-session, not per-command — the PTY is one long-lived process, so a
later `user` that disagrees is a 400. Linux only.

ShellSelector.description:
Which interpreter runs the command (the v2 `shell` selector).

`auto` is the platform-default chain (unix bash→sh, Windows
pwsh→powershell); the named selectors never fall back — asking for a shell
that is absent is an error, not a substitution. On Windows `bash` is Git
Bash and `cmd` runs the script as a batch file. `none` runs `command` as a
program with `args` as its argv: no shell, no quoting, no expansion.

input.description:
Written to the PTY verbatim, byte for byte — escape sequences and
control characters included, so `\u{1b}` is ESC and `\u{3}` is Ctrl-C.

press_enter.description:
Appends a carriage return (`0x0D`) — the byte the Enter key sends.
Canonical shells cannot tell it from `\n` (the tty's ICRNL maps CR to
NL), but raw-mode TUIs can: to them `\n` is Shift+Enter ("insert a
newline"), which is why this is CR. For a literal newline put `\n` in
`input` itself. Do not combine a trailing `\r` in `input` with
`press_enter: true` — that is Enter twice.

ref.description:
Stable element ref usable by click/fill/upload for the life of the
snapshot (the page's backend DOM node id). Absent for structural nodes.

truncated.description:
Root only: the page exceeded [`AX_MAX_NODES`] or [`AX_MAX_DEPTH`], so
what came back is a prefix of the tree, not the tree. Omitted when the
whole page fit, which keeps an untruncated snapshot byte-identical to
the shape clients already parse.

interactive_only.description: Prune to nodes with an actionable role (button/link/textbox/...).

home_dir.description:
1.x's name for the same directory, filled in on the `/v1` plane only:
the 1.x client model requires it. Absent from every other response.

oneOf.description:
The account `user` can name on the command planes, when the image
bakes one; `None` means it does not and everything runs as `user`.
Reported rather than assumed because neither the name nor the uid is a
contract — `ensure-user.sh` records whatever it actually resolved, since
1000 may already be taken.

Wire-compat names for one value: the daemon account's home, which is
where a command that names no working directory runs. The daemon has no
configurable workspace; these fields are kept because clients read them
to learn that directory.

How much the backend could actually see for a window.

Three-state rather than a boolean: an application with no accessibility
implementation returns an `Empty` subtree, which is materially different
from a rich one and must not be reported as success. A client that gets
`empty` should fall back to pixels for that window rather than conclude the
window has no controls.

selector.description: CSS selector of the `<input type=file>` (A-class path).

WindowRefAction.description: Addresses a window from a `GET /v2/computer/windows` listing.

WindowSummary.description:
One enumerated window.

`window_id` is valid only within the snapshot that produced it — a handle
that outlives its listing would silently operate on whatever now occupies
it. (Accessibility `node_id`s are backend handles and do outlive theirs.)

oneOf.description:
Absolute screen coordinates — the same space as the cursor, screenshots
and the accessibility tree, so a caller can move to a window's centre
without converting anything.

info.description:
The current API surface of the aiod sandbox daemon. Every route is served by one process inside the sandbox; nothing here is a wrapper over an older namespace.

**Core** — `health`, `sandbox`, `commands`, `fs`, `watch`, `pty` — is served by every daemon on every platform it supports, with `pty` the one exception (Unix only). `GET /v2/sandbox` describes the environment and its capabilities in a single call, which is the intended first request.

**Detected capabilities** — `code`, `browser`, `computer` — are lit by what the daemon finds at startup rather than by configuration. Where a backend is absent the routes stay listed and answer 503, so a client can branch on the capability probe instead of on a 404.

The daemon trusts its network: authentication is a single optional `AIO_API_KEY` (`Authorization: Bearer`, `x-api-key`, or `?api_key=`), and when it is unset the port answers whoever reaches it — put the daemon behind a gateway you control.

The `/v1/*` compatibility surface is documented separately at `/v1/openapi.json`.

post.description:
A stateless JSON-RPC 2.0 subset — initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call —
answered as JSON, with no event stream and no session state. A notification
